principles: Additive, not mutative: introduce a NEW aggregate; never redefine the strict four-field providerReportedTotal/known semantics.
Never infer an unreported value: a null input OR output excludes the record from the primary total; cacheCreation/cacheRead are never coerced to 0.
Keep informational-only informational-only: the new field feeds no gate and carries no gate/verdict/decision name.
Preserve module isolation: only ./ sibling + node: imports inside usage-ledger.
Parallel structure: model the primary aggregate symmetrically to the existing total so the code and tests read the same way.
drivers: Audit rule: the ledger must never invent a token count a provider did not report (the whole reason cache-less records are 'unknown' today).
Backward compatibility: existing summary/diagnostics consumers and their invariants (providerReportedTotal, known rollups, cost) must be byte-for-byte unchanged.
Operator visibility: codex/gemini input+output spend must show up somewhere in the report instead of vanishing into an unknown bucket.

options.name: primary-total
pros: Surfaces codex/gemini input+output without touching cacheCreation/cacheRead — no inference.
Strict four-field providerReportedTotal/known/cost stay exactly as-is (purely additive).
input/output are validator-guaranteed non-null for provider-reported, so the primary total is always defined for them.
Symmetric to existing total/known, low cognitive overhead, easy to test with a clean negative assertion.
cons: Adds new fields to UsageSummary and SourceTokenTotals (shape grows; consumers verified to not deepEqual the whole object).
Two totals now coexist (primary vs four-field) — must be documented so operators don't conflate them.

options.name: cacheCreation-known-zero-adapter-rule
pros: No new aggregate fields; codex/gemini would flow into the existing providerReportedTotal.
cons: Mutates the strict four-field meaning: declares a value (cacheCreation=0) the provider never reported — violates the no-inference audit rule.
Still incomplete: cacheRead can be null when prompt_tokens_details/cachedContentTokenCount is absent, so the record can STILL be unknown.
Touches the adapters (out of scope) and risks contaminating cost derivation with an invented 0.
Higher blast radius on existing invariants/tests.

rationale: The primary-total approach is the only one that satisfies the hard audit constraint (never infer an unreported value) while still making codex/gemini input+output visible. It is purely additive, leaves the strict four-field providerReportedTotal/known/cost semantics and the adapters untouched, and is robust to cacheRead also being null. The cacheCreation=0 adapter rule both violates the no-inference rule and fails to fully solve the problem (null cacheRead), so it is rejected.

preMortem.scenario: The new primary aggregate silently double-counts or mis-buckets estimate/unavailable records.
preMortem.trigger: Accumulating primaryKnown without re-checking source, or summing primaryReportedTotal over non-provider-reported records.
preMortem.consequence: primaryReportedTotal becomes a meaningless mixed number; operators distrust the report.
preMortem.mitigation: Gate primaryReportedTotal on source==='provider-reported' (mirroring providerReportedTotal); exclude source==='unavailable' from the per-source primary accumulation; add a smoke asserting estimate/unavailable do NOT contribute.

preMortem.scenario: An existing invariant regresses because providerReportedTotal/known/cost behavior shifted.
preMortem.trigger: Refactoring the shared accumulation loop and accidentally changing the four-field path.
preMortem.consequence: Prior smokes (usage-ledger-smoke, estimate-smoke, diagnostics-smoke, codex-gemini-smoke) fail or, worse, pass with wrong numbers.
preMortem.mitigation: Make the change strictly additive (new branches/fields only); run the FULL smoke suite green; keep the existing assertions (unknownCount unchanged for codex/gemini, providerReportedTotal excludes them) intact.

preMortem.scenario: The added fields break the module isolation or the report's no-gate invariant.
preMortem.trigger: Importing a helper from outside usage-ledger, or naming a field with a banned gate/verdict/decision token.
preMortem.consequence: The static zero-cross-module-import check or the no-gate deep-key scan fails, blocking the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement asPrimaryDimensions inside diagnostics.ts; name fields primaryReportedTotal/primaryKnown/primaryKnownCount (no banned tokens); rely on the existing static smokes to confirm.
